_why: Ceilings for the whole bridge; both tiers are checked in 2026, 1894 and 1940 (period eras add meshes); shared with the terrain and city tiles; check.mjs prints both tables. full (laptops): draw calls bind first in WebGL, ~1,500/frame at 60 fps on an Iris Xe/GTX 1650/M1-class GPU; every shadow caster is drawn twice and the tiles take several hundred, so the bridge gets 300 (~600 with shadows). Triangles: 1 M plus the tiles, doubled by the shadow pass, is ~3-4 M/frame, comfortable on that class. lite (judges' phones, look/tier.js, ?lite=1): a mid phone (Adreno 6xx, A13-A15) holds 60 fps at roughly 300-500 calls and ~1 M triangles per frame all in, so the bridge's fair share is ~150 calls; it spent 230 before static parts merged per material on LITE (<Part merge>, now 193). The lite cap therefore freezes it near today (240 calls, ~4% over today; 260 k triangles, the busiest year (1940, period traffic) + 20%): new geometry-heavy detail must be skipped when LITE is true, and lite should shrink towards 150. baseline: [draw calls, triangles] per part id on main at 2026-11-01, for the deltas in the tables; update it when you land a deliberate spend.
_why1890: 1890 (stage 2, full tier): per half, a derrick (mast, slewing jib, rope, hook: 4 calls, split only where a piece animates) and the timber centring (1). check.mjs fails if a works-* part draws more calls than this.
